LCD1602.SECTION_BUS_DOC: Where the display hangs and what it is. Leave the type and addresses on Automatic for a Waveshare, Grove or DFRobot module, or a common I2C backpack; choose them by hand when Detect names something else.
LCD1602.I2C_MODE_DOC: The hardware bus on GPIO 2 and 3 serves nearly every wiring. The second hardware bus and the software bus need a line in /boot/userconfig.txt, written when you save, and a restart.
LCD1602.I2C_HARDWARE: Hardware bus 1 (GPIO 2 SDA, GPIO 3 SCL; pins 3 and 5)
LCD1602.I2C_HARDWARE0: Hardware bus 0 (GPIO 0 SDA, GPIO 1 SCL; pins 27 and 28)
LCD1602.I2C_SOFTWARE: Software bus on chosen pins (slower, any two GPIOs)
LCD1602.SDA_PIN_DOC: BCM GPIO number for the data line of the software bus.
LCD1602.SCL_PIN_DOC: BCM GPIO number for the clock line of the software bus.
LCD1602.PANEL_TYPE_DOC: AiP31068: Waveshare LCD1602 I2C and RGB, Grove LCD RGB, DFRobot RGB LCD. ST7032: Midas, Newhaven C0216CiZ and other modules with a contrast register (same address as the AiP31068, so it has to be chosen). US2066: Winstar and Newhaven character OLEDs over I2C. PCF8574 backpack: the common adapter board soldered to a parallel 1602. Winstar OLED on a backpack: a WS0010 module behind the same adapter.
LCD1602.PANEL_WS0010: Winstar WS0010 OLED on a PCF8574 backpack
LCD1602.PANEL_ADDRESS_DOC: Automatic tries 0x3E, 0x27, 0x3F, 0x3C and 0x3D. Detect lists what answers on the bus.
LCD1602.PCF_PINMAP_DOC: Backpacks only. Standard: RS, RW, E and the backlight on P0 to P3, data on P4 to P7. Alternate: data on P0 to P3 (mjkdz and similar). Garbled characters on a backpack usually mean the other layout.
LCD1602.CONTRAST_DOC: ST7032 modules set their contrast in software, 0 to 63; around 40 suits 3.3 V.
LCD1602.RGB_ADDRESS_DOC: Automatic finds the PCA9633 of the Waveshare and Grove modules and the DFRobot drivers. None for a module without an RGB backlight.
LCD1602.DETECT_DOC: Scan the bus and name what answers.
LCD1602.TEST_DOC: Put a test pattern on the display for a few seconds.
LCD1602.DETECTED_NOTHING: Nothing answers on bus {{bus}}. Check the wiring, VCC and GND, and that I2C is enabled.
LCD1602.DETECT_FAILED: The bus could not be scanned: {{error}}
LCD1602.TEST_SENT: The test pattern is on the display.
LCD1602.TEST_FAILED: The display daemon did not answer: {{error}}
LCD1602.SECTION_METER_DOC: How the bars follow the music.
LCD1602.GAIN_DOC: Added to the measured level before it is drawn, -12 to +12 dB. Raise it for quiet material, lower it when the bars sit at the top.
LCD1602.SOURCE_DOC: RMS is the loudness a VU meter shows; peak follows every transient.
LCD1602.RANGE_DOC: How many decibels the bar spans below full scale. 40 suits most music; 60 shows quiet passages.
LCD1602.BAR_STYLE_DOC: Blocks: a solid bar, 75 steps across. Lines: three thin lines a cell. Segments: two broad segments a cell, like an LED chain. Needle: a single line at the level.
LCD1602.PEAK_HOLD_DOC: A marker that stays at the highest level for a moment, then falls.
LCD1602.PEAK_HOLD_MS_DOC: How long the marker holds before it falls.
LCD1602.LABELS_DOC: A letter before each bar; without them the bars take the whole row.
LCD1602.FPS_DOC: How often the display is redrawn, 5 to 30. A software I2C bus or a backpack may want fewer.
LCD1602.SECTION_IDLE_DOC: What the display shows while nothing plays.
LCD1602.PAUSE_STANDBY_DOC: Volumio's play button pauses rather than stops, so a paused player is the usual resting state. On, a pause is treated as a stop after the seconds below: the standby rows and colour, then the backlight off after the seconds set at the end of this section. Off, the pause message (or the still bars) stays until the player stops or plays.
LCD1602.PAUSE_TIMEOUT_DOC: 0 shows standby the moment the player pauses; a few seconds show the pause message first. Playing again brings the bars back at once.
LCD1602.IDLE_LAYOUT_DOC: Two rows, each chosen below, or the time in large digits across both rows.
LCD1602.IDLE_TEXT_DOC: The text rows, first and second separated by |, 16 characters each.
LCD1602.CLOCK_FORMAT_DOC: For the clock rows and the large clock; a twelve-hour format puts AM or PM beside the large digits.
LCD1602.DATE_FORMAT_DOC: For the date rows, in the player's language where the format names the day or the month.
LCD1602.IDLE_OFF_DOC: Seconds of standby after which the backlight goes dark; 0 keeps it on. It comes back when music plays.
LCD1602.SECTION_MESSAGES_DOC: What the display says as the player boots, stands ready, pauses, restarts and shuts down. Two rows, separated by |.
LCD1602.SHOW_LIFECYCLE_DOC: Off: the display shows standby while booting and the bars while paused, and clears when the system goes down.
LCD1602.SECTION_RGB_DOC: For modules with an RGB backlight. A plain backlight is on while these colours are not black.
LCD1602.RGB_MODE_DOC: Fixed: the colour below. Level: from green through amber to red with the music. Off: the backlight stays dark.
LCD1602.RGB_HEX_DOC: Six hex digits, RRGGBB: FFFFFF white, FF8000 orange, 0040FF blue.
LCD1602.SAVED_RESTART: Settings saved. The I2C bus changed in /boot/userconfig.txt; restart the player for it to take effect.
LCD1602.SAVE_FAILED: The settings could not be saved: {{error}}
LCD1602.BAD_COLOR: {{field}} is not a colour: use six hex digits, RRGGBB.
LCD1602.SERVICE_FAILED: The display service could not be started: {{error}}
LCD1602.RESTART_MSG: The audio tap joins the player's output chain at the next restart. Until then the display shows the player's state but no levels.
